plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with narrow gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated for its essential oil and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy sepals. It thrives in partial shade and moist soil and is a staple of cottage and woodland gardens.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in temperate gardens across Europe, North America, and the Azores
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue blooms while alkaline soils produce pink.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tropical tree with fern-like leaves and a canopy covered in brilliant clusters of orange-red flowers. It is often planted as a shade tree along streets and in parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: May through July in the Northern Hemisphere tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated in India, the Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Africa, and Florida
plants.funFact: Despite being one of the most celebrated tropical trees worldwide, it is endangered in its native Madagascar.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged Australian tree or shrub with serrated leathery leaves and cylindrical flower spikes made of thousands of tiny flowers. It provides nectar for birds, bats, and insects during the cooler months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowers present from late autumn through July
plants.location: Eastern Australia, from Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: The woody seed cones inspired the 'Banksia men' characters in May Gibbs' classic Australian children's book Snugglepot and Cuddlepie.
